title: Visual outcomes and complications of manual small-incision cataract surgery in patients with pseudoexfoliation

license.statement: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 (article <license>); not CC BY, record kept private

indication: Cataract with pseudoexfoliation (unilateral 28, bilateral 124 of 152 patients); immature, mature, brown, hypermature and black cataracts and 2 phacolytic glaucoma; traumatic, complicated and uveitic cataract, corneal scars and previous ocular surgery excluded

groups.description: Manual small-incision cataract surgery with PMMA IOL by one senior surgeon, standard care; pupil-expansion measures, CTR or anterior vitrectomy when needed

series.baseline_label: Preoperative ECD of the operated eye (Topcon SP3000P specular microscope)
series.notes: mean (SD) [range]; per-visit n not tabulated for ECD

exclusions.reason: number of cells counted, not cell density
change derived from the same series; the absolute ECD series is used

notes: Prospective observational study (December 2016 to November 2017), 152 eyes of 152 patients, follow-up day 1, 1 week, 1 month and 3 months; specular microscopy preoperatively and at 1 and 3 months.
Table 3 (BCVA) accounts for all 152 patients at each visit; the ECD table gives no per-visit n.
The article does not state that the 7 eyes with intraoperative complications (zonular dialysis 5, posterior capsule rupture 1, iridodialysis 1) were left out of Table 4.
